requiredEnvironments.label: Windows Firefox or Chromium with NVDA
Physical iPhone or iPad Safari with VoiceOver
Browser zoom and reflow at 200% and 400%
macOS increased contrast or Windows high contrast

scenarios.title: Docs landmarks, navigation, search, appearance controls, and page actions
steps: Navigate landmarks, headings, sidebar, search, table of contents, links, and page actions.
Change theme, mode, and density, then move between documentation routes.
Confirm focus order, visible focus, names, announcements, and route-change context.
expected: Navigation is understandable without visual position or color.
Focus order follows the reading order and remains visible.
Search, appearance controls, and page actions expose stable names and state.

scenarios.title: Representative product composition, responsive navigation, and safe areas
steps: Navigate the desktop workspace and its mobile drill-in flow.
Open and dismiss responsive navigation and task overlays.
Inspect safe-area spacing, focus restoration, and reflow at narrow widths.
expected: Responsive composition preserves content, controls, and logical focus.
Modal surfaces contain focus and restore it to the invoking control.
Safe areas and reflow do not hide actions or status.

scenarios.title: Button, icon action, loading, disabled, and Toggle pressed state
steps: Activate text, icon-only, loading, disabled, grouped, and pressed controls.
Confirm stable names while loading and pressed state changes.
Verify Enter, Space, pointer, and touch behavior where available.
expected: Momentary, loading, disabled, and retained pressed states remain distinct.
Icon-only actions have stable accessible names independent of Tooltip.
State and focus remain perceivable without color alone.

scenarios.title: Field relationships, validation, grouped controls, and native form behavior
steps: Navigate labels, descriptions, required fields, invalid fields, and grouped controls.
Change Checkbox, RadioGroup, Switch, and Select values using native keyboard and touch models.
Confirm validation and help text are announced once and remain associated.
expected: Every control has a stable name and applicable description or error relationship.
Required, invalid, checked, selected, disabled, and read-only states are announced.
Keyboard and touch interaction match the documented control semantics.

scenarios.title: Native date, month, week, time, and datetime-local inputs
steps: Focus each supported temporal input and use the platform picker.
Enter, change, clear, and submit representative values.
Inspect localized picker chrome, constraints, validity, and focus return.
expected: The browser-owned picker remains operable and understandable.
Value, constraint, validity, reset, and submission behavior remain native.
Mobile picker dismissal restores usable focus and viewport state.

scenarios.title: Slider keyboard, touch, pointer, orientation, RTL, and value text
steps: Change values with Arrow, Page, Home, End, pointer, and touch input.
Inspect horizontal, vertical, disabled, read-only, and RTL behavior.
Confirm value text and orientation are announced.
expected: Value changes are predictable and bounded by the documented constraints.
Touch and keyboard interaction expose the same value contract.
Focus, value, orientation, and disabled state remain perceivable without color.

scenarios.title: FileInput selection, announcement, reset, and mobile picker
steps: Open the native picker for single, multiple, and capture-capable inputs.
Select files, inspect filename announcement, and reset the form.
Cancel the picker and confirm focus and viewport restoration.
expected: The native picker, selected filenames, constraints, and reset remain understandable.
Cancel and selection restore focus to the input.
No upload, validation workflow, or storage behavior is implied.

scenarios.title: Calendar grid navigation, constraints, locale, RTL, and announcements
steps: Navigate days, weeks, months, and years using the documented keyboard model.
Inspect today, selected, outside-month, unavailable, disabled, and read-only dates.
Repeat representative navigation with locale and RTL changes.
expected: Roving focus and month changes remain predictable and announced.
Localized date names and selected state remain understandable.
Constraints prevent selection without removing navigation context.

scenarios.title: DatePicker opening, Calendar interaction, clear, dismissal, and form value
steps: Open the picker, navigate the Calendar, select and clear a date.
Dismiss with Escape, outside interaction, and the documented close path.
Inspect form value, validation, mobile viewport pressure, and focus restoration.
expected: Opening transfers focus into the Calendar and dismissal restores it.
Display text and submitted YYYY-MM-DD value remain aligned.
Clear, constraints, required, invalid, and read-only behavior remain understandable.

scenarios.title: Heading, list, table, item, and overflow semantics
steps: Navigate headings, lists, linked Items, table captions, headers, rows, and actions.
Focus and scroll the named table overflow region.
Inspect selected, current, disabled-looking, long, localized, and narrow content.
expected: Document, list, link, and table relationships remain understandable.
Overflow is keyboard reachable without trapping focus.
Selection, current state, and actions do not depend on row color alone.

scenarios.title: Alert, Toast, progress, loading, empty, and error announcements
steps: Trigger low- and high-priority feedback, actions, dismissal, loading, and empty states.
Inspect announcement timing, repetition, urgency, and focus behavior.
Repeat with reduced motion and increased or high contrast.
expected: Feedback is announced with appropriate urgency without duplicate speech.
Actions and dismissal remain keyboard and touch operable.
Loading, progress, status, and empty meaning do not depend on animation or color.

scenarios.title: Tabs, Breadcrumbs, and Pagination navigation models
steps: Navigate Tabs in both orientations, including disabled items.
Inspect Breadcrumbs and Pagination current-page semantics.
Repeat with long labels, narrow width, and RTL where applicable.
expected: Tabs expose orientation, selection, and the expected arrow-key model.
Only one breadcrumb or pagination item is current.
Navigation remains usable when wrapped or reflowed.

scenarios.title: Command query, active descendant, live states, and Sidebar collapse
steps: Search, navigate groups, select a result, and inspect loading and empty states.
Collapse and expand Sidebar, then inspect trigger naming, inert content, and focus retention.
Repeat the mobile Sidebar path through Sheet.
expected: Command keeps DOM focus and active-descendant context predictable.
Loading, empty, selection, and result counts are concise and non-duplicative.
Collapsed or hidden Sidebar content is not interactable.

scenarios.title: Dialog, Sheet, Popover, Tooltip, and Dropdown Menu focus and dismissal
steps: Open each overlay with keyboard and touch or pointer input.
Navigate content, exercise close paths, and inspect nested overlay behavior.
Confirm focus containment where modal, dismissal, scroll lock, and restoration.
expected: Modal and non-modal overlay semantics remain distinct.
Every overlay has an understandable name and predictable dismissal path.
Focus, scroll, viewport, and trigger context are restored after dismissal.

scenarios.title: Optional Motion adapter preference changes and static end states
steps: Load the Motion adapter examples with reduced motion enabled before navigation.
Change the operating-system preference while the page remains open.
Trigger entry, exit, and visibility examples with and without the preference.
expected: User-preference reduced motion removes animated transform and layout travel.
Static end states, content order, focus, and useful visibility feedback remain intact.
Live preference changes apply without reload, hydration error, or duplicate announcement.

scenarios.title: Themes, modes, density, RTL, reduced motion, and contrast
steps: Inspect representative surfaces across six themes, light and dark, both densities, and RTL.
Enable reduced motion before load and while the app is open.
Inspect focus, selected, current, invalid, disabled, and destructive states at high contrast.
expected: Runtime axes do not change component semantics or reading order.
Reduced-motion preference removes nonessential CSS motion.
Focus and state remain perceivable under increased or high contrast.
